headline: P0009 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share is elevated in every complexity group, but the sampled documentation supports the billed levels, including on several low-complexity 99215 claims
rationale: P0009 billed 99215 on 13.8% of 145 claims, against an expected 2.5% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 3.19; z vs peers 1.27). The excess shows up across all complexity groups, including patients with 0 chronic conditions (7.1% vs 2.1% for all providers) and 1 condition (13.0% vs 3.4%). On claims alone, that would be a concern. The records review points the other way. Of 39 documented claims, none of the 5 documented 99215s was unsupported (all-provider rate 24.2%), none of 20 documented 99214s was unsupported (all-provider rate 8.4%), and 1 of 12 documented 99213s was unsupported (8.3% vs 7.5%). Several sampled 99215s on low-complexity patients have documented high MDM and 40 or more minutes: C0003234 (asthma, 42 min), C0003259 (no chronic conditions, 49 min) and C0003327 (no chronic conditions, 40 min). C0003219 is also documented as high MDM with 41 minutes. Overall the pattern is more consistent with visits that were truly complex than with upcoding. The caveat is that only 5 of the 20 99215 claims were documented, so the evidence leans this way without being conclusive. The rest of the low-complexity 99215s, such as C0003213, C0003216, C0003217, C0003235, C0003267, C0003305 and C0003325, have not been reviewed.
next_steps: Pull records for the undocumented 99215 claims, starting with low-complexity patients (C0003213, C0003216, C0003217, C0003235, C0003267, C0003305, C0003325), to grow the documented 99215 sample beyond 5.

Check whether the 99215s on patients with 0 to 1 chronic conditions reflect acute problems not captured in the chronic-condition counts (for example the R10.9 and R21 diagnoses), which would explain high MDM.
Check the repeat 99215 visits by the same patients (P0009-N0049 on C0003267 and C0003327; P0009-N0036 on C0003210 and C0003330) for consistent, non-templated documentation.
Re-score after the larger documentation sample. If the 99215 unsupported rate stays well below the 24.2% all-provider rate, consider closing the case as a legitimately complex panel.
